packages/cli/package.json -- confirmed no 'open' npm dependency was added; deliberate choice per comment at open-browser.ts:4-5

NEW BUG: packages/cli/src/utils/open-browser.ts:12-24 -- only the synchronous spawn() call is wrapped in try/catch; there is no child.on('error', ...) listener. child_process.spawn reports a missing executable (ENOENT) via an ASYNCHRONOUS 'error' event, not a synchronous throw -- with no listener attached, Node's EventEmitter rethrows it as an uncaught exception. Confirmed no process-level 'uncaughtException'/'unhandledRejection' handler exists anywhere in packages/cli/src (grep returned zero matches). Concrete risk: xdg-open is commonly absent on a headless Linux VPS/container reached over SSH -- exactly the environment the CLI's own docker-compose deploy target is aimed at -- so a successful install can crash the CLI process one tick after printing its success message, contradicting the documented 'best-effort, never throws' contract in the function's own comment.

FIXED (commit 4579870): packages/cli/src/utils/open-browser.ts:20-24 -- spawn()'s returned ChildProcess now has child.on('error', () => {}) attached before child.unref(), so an asynchronous ENOENT (e.g. missing xdg-open on a headless host) is consumed by the listener instead of becoming an uncaught exception. Function's own 'never throws' contract (doc comment) is now actually upheld for the async failure path, not just the synchronous spawn() call already wrapped in try/catch.
